quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 results (CEO Patrice Caine / CFO Jeremy Papin): order intake EUR 12.5 billion, up 22% organically, book-to-bill 1.14; sales EUR 10.9 billion, up 7.8% organically (9.6% excluding the cancellation of two geostationary telecom satellites, which cut sales by EUR 153 million); adjusted EBIT nearly EUR 1.4 billion, up 10% (11% organic), margin 12.5%; adjusted net income group share EUR 990 million, up 13%. Free operating cash flow was EUR 1.8 billion per the CEO (close to three times H1 2025; the CFO cited EUR 1.9 billion versus half a billion), and net debt was EUR 519 million at June 2026 versus EUR 1.6 billion at December 31, 2025. Europe sales +9.4% organic, emerging markets +14.6%, Middle East +36.7%.
quarterly_data.figure: orders EUR 12.5 billion (+22%); sales EUR 10.9 billion (+7.8% organic); adjusted EBIT margin 12.5%; adjusted net income EUR 990 million (+13%); net debt EUR 519 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance (CEO Patrice Caine): organic sales growth of 6%-7%, corresponding to sales of EUR 23.3 billion-EUR 23.6 billion, confirmed; adjusted EBIT margin expected between 12.6%-12.8%; two items upgraded a couple of weeks before the call - book-to-bill now above 1.1 and adjusted net income to free operating cash flow conversion of 100%-110%. CFO: 2026 CapEx guidance still roughly EUR 850 million (higher in H2); the additional French corporate tax is expected at nearly EUR 100 million in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: sales EUR 23.3 billion-EUR 23.6 billion (6%-7% organic); adjusted EBIT margin 12.6%-12.8%; book-to-bill above 1.1; CapEx roughly EUR 850 million

quarterly_data.signal: Order intake detail (CFO Jeremy Papin): 18 large orders above EUR 100 million in H1 (7 in Q1, 11 in Q2), 13 of them in defense (including air defense, air surveillance and air traffic management) and five in space; orders below EUR 10 million up 5% organically. CEO: major contracts included satellites for Luxembourg and Turkey, air surveillance systems for Qatar and radars for the UAE; Europe order intake was up 46% organically; he expects strong, robust defense order momentum for the full year from Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Southeast Asia.
quarterly_data.figure: 18 large orders (13 defense, 5 space); Europe orders +46% organic

quarterly_data.signal: Defense segment H1 2026 (CFO Jeremy Papin): orders EUR 7.4 billion, up 28%, with 13 large contracts (six a year earlier), including two large orders for development of the Rafale F5 standard; sales EUR 6.3 billion, up 13% organically (Q2 +11.9%) on the production ramp-up in sensors and effectors; adjusted EBIT up 22% organically, margin 13.8% (12.8% a year earlier). CFO: the defense revenue outlook has moved from high single-digit to a low double-digit growth potential, and the margin can stay above 13.5%. CEO: the SAMP/T NG outperforms Patriot and is available around 2028 versus around 2032 for Patriot, with prospects including Ukraine, Greece, Nordic countries and the Middle East.
quarterly_data.figure: defense orders EUR 7.4 billion (+28%); sales EUR 6.3 billion (+13%); margin 13.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Aerospace segment H1 2026 (CFO Jeremy Papin): orders EUR 3.3 billion, up 24% organically, including five large space contracts (geostationary telecom satellites for Luxembourg and Qatar, Copernicus, ExoMars); sales EUR 2.8 billion, up 2.1% organically (8.8% excluding the satellite cancellation); adjusted EBIT margin 10.4%, up 130 bps. Space profitability turned positive and space growth is expected to be low single digit for the rest of the year; the CEO targets a linear progression to around 7% space operating margin by 2027. Avionics original equipment follows Airbus and Boeing production rates (the CEO says Thales is not the bottleneck for Airbus), while lower air traffic in the Middle East slightly reduced aftermarket activity. CEO on IRIS2: contracts expected soon.
quarterly_data.figure: aerospace orders EUR 3.3 billion (+24%); sales EUR 2.8 billion (+2.1%); margin 10.4%; space margin around 7% by 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Cyber and Digital H1 2026 (CFO Jeremy Papin): sales EUR 1.8 billion, up 0.4%; cyber up 1.6% organically (Q2 +4.5%) with adjusted EBIT up 5.5% and a 14% margin, expected at low-to-mid single digit growth for the full year; digital identity broadly flat; payment cards hit by lower volumes and prices. About two and a half points of the segment margin decline came from H1 2025 one-offs and another 30 to 40 bps from Forex; digital margin is expected to rebound to the 12%+ level for the full year. CEO: the payment business is around EUR 1 billion, with digital around 10%.
quarterly_data.figure: Cyber and Digital sales EUR 1.8 billion (+0.4%); cyber margin 14%; payment business around EUR 1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Security products (CEO Patrice Caine): Thales is expanding its cyber portfolio with a next-generation hardware security module, Luna 8, a new data security posture management solution, and a forthcoming AI Security Fabric solution expected in 2027; he says AI is accelerating demand for detection and response, application security and data protection.

Strategy and investments (CEO Patrice Caine / CFO Jeremy Papin): in H1 Thales announced the planned acquisition of Exail (autonomous underwater warfare and inertial navigation), new partnerships for counter-UAS, air defense and mass production, and an enlarged trusted-cloud partnership in Germany. R&D rose 9% to 6.2% of sales and is not capitalized; restructuring costs fell to EUR 24 million as the space adaptation plan is complete; the effective tax rate was 25.8% (21% excluding the temporary additional French corporate tax of EUR 57 million in H1).
quarterly_data.figure: R&D 6.2% of sales (+9%); restructuring EUR 24 million; effective tax rate 25.8%
